project.name: ĀML™ — ĀRU Meaning Language™
project.status: working research prototype and evolving specification

principle: Do not begin with a platform rewrite. Begin with a falsifiable interface decision.

stages.name: understand
stages.goal: Understand AML's category and claim boundary before evaluation.

stages.name: reproduce-one-decision
stages.goal: Reproduce a deterministic ALLOW/SUPPRESS decision and inspect the evidence.

stages.name: evaluate-contract
stages.goal: Test repository claims and software behavior before discussing deployment.

stages.name: integrate-narrowly
stages.goal: Integrate one bounded surface without a platform rewrite.

stages.name: shadow
stages.goal: Observe AML decisions without changing production behavior.

stages.name: canary
stages.goal: Enforce AML only on a reversible bounded surface with explicit rollback criteria.

stages.name: independent-verification
stages.goal: Obtain reproduction outside the implementation path.

stages.name: production-readiness
stages.goal: Decide whether the evaluated deployment is operationally and security-ready.

stages.name: publish-evidence
stages.goal: Publish scoped results without turning a pilot into a universal claim.

nonclaims: AML is not represented as a ratified global standard.
AML is not represented as universally adopted infrastructure.
AML does not claim objective scientific measurement of cognition or wellbeing.
AML does not replace a production security stack.
AML does not guarantee safe, ethical, legal, or compliant interfaces.
